music.title: Les Danaïdes
music.description: Salieri's opera needs Aegyptus' fifty sons as the bridegrooms — the twin brother's claim that drives Danaus' flight and the wedding-night massacre.

popCulture.title: The Suppliants
popCulture.creator: Aeschylus
popCulture.description: Aeschylus keeps Aegyptus offstage but present: his sons pursue the Danaids to Argos, and the king's will is the force the suppliants flee.

popCulture.title: Aegyptus
popCulture.description: The eponymous twin of Danaus — king of Egypt whose fifty sons chase the fifty Danaids — remains the other half of the Argive foundation myth.

popCulture.title: Danaïdes
popCulture.description: The murdered sons of Aegyptus haunt the Danaid story: their wedding night becomes the underworld's leaking jars, and his name survives in their crime.
